boundary_decision.rationale: The root is a versioned instrument aggregate that owns questions, response structures, logic and presentation variants. Study, campaign, wave, administration, interview, respondent, consent, sample, actual response, dataset and result remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: Survey study and collection activity remain separate from the reusable questionnaire instrument even when the package binds their intended use.
No relation row is frozen; the parent signal grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.
Question definition, permitted response domain, actual answer, respondent, observation, dataset value and analyst inference remain independently identifiable.
Every variant is versioned because wording, order, translation, device, channel and interviewer behavior can change meaning and comparability.
The instrument declares deterministic logic and seeds but does not execute a collection session or create an answer.
Missing, do not know, refusal, not applicable, not asked, invalid, incomplete and nonresponse are distinct states.
Cognitive, pilot, usability, accessibility, reliability, validity and bias claims remain method, population, mode, version, source and limitation qualified.
Sensitive questions, consent, contact, identity linkage, disclosure and retention require accountable external authority.
FHIR is healthcare Trial Use; Census, Statistics Canada, GOV.UK, AAPOR and GSBPM are sector profiles. ISO 20252 claims are limited to public metadata.

One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audits the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts; assurance remains reviewable-draft.

deferred_research: Approve or reject the WM-REC-007 relation and register Study, Campaign, Wave, Administration, Respondent, Consent, Sample, Response, Dataset, Variable and Analysis edges.
Create domain, jurisdiction, psychometric, clinical, educational, polling, adaptive-testing, accessibility, consent, privacy and organizational profiles.
Conformance-test question identity, response domains, routing, randomization, calculations, translations and mode variants against concrete authoring and collection engines.
Validate organization-specific respondent communication, sampling, ethics, identity-linkage, disclosure, legal hold, retention and disposition policies.
Inspect licensed ISO requirements under authorized access before making clause-level conformance claims.
Obtain independent external review before promoting beyond reviewable-draft assurance.
publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-DAT-009 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external research result was admitted.
Relation hold: no relation row is frozen and the WM-REC-007 parent signal grants no approved ownership, mutation or cascade behavior.

Boundary hold: survey study, questionnaire instrument, campaign, wave, administration, interview, respondent, consent, sample, response, observation, dataset and result must remain separate identities.
Meaning hold: wording, response domain, language, mode, order, routing, randomization, calculation and presentation variants require explicit compatibility evidence.

Authority hold: respondent contact, publication, ethics approval, consent, sampling changes, answer collection, trait inference, identity linkage, access widening, dataset creation, result certification and records disposition require delegated authority.

Privacy hold: unreleased instruments, sampling or anti-fraud logic, respondent identifiers, consent details, actual answers, sensitive-trait mappings and restricted tests require purpose-bound access and minimization.
Restricted-source hold: ISO 20252:2026 is used only from public scope and lifecycle metadata; access-restricted clauses were not inspected or inferred.

Interoperability hold: every DDI, GSIM, GSBPM, ISO, FHIR, Census, WCAG, DPV, PROV, SKOS, time and language projection requires release pins, conformance tests, mapping provenance and information-loss declarations.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
